meta.note: Source register for the prototype. Every claim on a profile points to one or more of these IDs. All entries were read on the 'accessed' date; none are community-held or private documents.

sources.title: Kira Becomes First Protected Area in Malaita Province
sources.date: Page metadata 8 Nov 2023; ceremony year not stated in text
sources.notes: Ceremony dates (27-28 November) do not match the page's publication metadata, so the year of declaration is unconfirmed.

sources.title: Protected Area Registration: Kira Forest Biodiversity Conservation Area (KFBCA)
sources.notes: Government news item. Names officials and a site coordinator; individuals are not republished in this prototype.

sources.title: Kira Forest Biodiversity Conservation Area (portal entry)
sources.notes: Single news-style entry; no coordinates, boundary or IUCN category shown on the page read.

sources.title: Ahetaha Water Conservation Association (partner profile)
sources.publisher: Cultural Survival (Keepers of the Earth Fund)
sources.notes: Funder-side description of the group's work. Spelled 'Association' here; S02 writes 'Foundation'.

sources.title: Mai-Maasina Green Belt Acknowledges UNDP-GEF for Project Funding and Partnership
sources.notes: Does not state the size of the area. Unclear which funded works belong to Mai-Maasina Green Belt and which to its partner AWCA.

sources.title: New Association Launched to Protect East Are'Are Rainforests
sources.notes: Does not state area, office-holders or funders.

sources.title: Malaitans reap benefits from conserving marine areas
sources.notes: Mainly about Manaoba LMMA (Lau Lagoon, outside this atlas); one section covers Puriasi in East Are'are. Figures are 2020 or earlier.

sources.title: Takataka Bay (location entry)
sources.notes: Source of the bay-level coordinates (about 9.298 S, 161.242 E). Not a survey of any conservation boundary.

sources.title: Malaita Province (constituencies and 2019 population)
sources.notes: Background only. East Are'are 8,199 people; West Are'are 8,008; Small Malaita 16,146 (2019 census figures as quoted). Check against the census release before citing.

sources.title: Protected areas of Solomon Islands
sources.notes: Lists three Key Biodiversity Areas in Malaita Province (Langa Langa Lagoon, Lau Lagoon, Ndai); none in Are'are or Small Malaita.

sources.title: New conservation areas in Malaita and Bougainville
sources.notes: Kwaio conservation areas (Baru Conservation Alliance). Outside this atlas's constituencies; kept as a comparison.

sources.title: Community conservation areas (tag listing)
sources.notes: Lists Kira as the only Malaita/Are'are entry on the page read; describes Vuri Forest Conservation Area (Choiseul) as the country's 5th legal Protected Area.

sources.title: Unlocking the Tourism Potential of Malaita Province
sources.notes: Focuses on Langalanga Lagoon. Does not mention Are'are or Small Malaita.

sources.title: Protected Planet terms and conditions
sources.notes: Governs reuse of WDPA/WDPCA data: non-commercial use, no redistribution by downloads or downloadable interactive maps, required citation.

sources.title: Three ways SCALE-NRM supports locally led protection of forests and livelihoods in the Solomon Islands
sources.notes: Gives Kira as 667 ha and a declaration date of 29 Oct 2023; also gives a celebration date of 27 Nov 2023 that conflicts with other sources.

sources.title: Kira Forest Biodiversity Conservation Area, first in Malaita
sources.notes: Publication date makes a late-November 2023 ceremony impossible. Text says 'Friday 27th to Saturday 28th November', which fits 27-28 October 2023.

sources.title: Takataka Eco Village Conservation Foundation
sources.notes: Contains a copy-paste error: some impact sections describe a Colombian project and were ignored.

sources.title: Kira Carbon Project
sources.notes: Project developer's page. Gives 661 ha. Carbon credit figure is an estimate.

sources.title: Safeguard social assessment: The Leather Back Turtle (Wai-Hau Conservation Foundation)
sources.date: Not stated; refers to events to 2015
sources.notes: Places the project in West Are'are on Aena'ura tribal land.

sources.title: Building capacity for monitoring and management of leatherback turtles in Are'are
sources.notes: States location as West 'Are'are.

sources.title: Detailed final report, leatherback monitoring at Waisurione
sources.notes: Names tribal lands as Ausi (Wairaha), Au'vaura (Waisurione) and Po'otori (Hauhui). S19 spells the second 'Aena'ura'.

sources.title: Mangrove Ecosystem Conservation, a Way Forward for South Malaita Tribal Community
sources.notes: Source for AHNRA. Does not give an area or a mangrove health assessment.

sources.title: Local Wisdom, Global Impact: Celebrating the Mai-Maasina Green Belt on World Environment Day
sources.notes: Describes a network of about thirty tribal communities across Are'are, Kwaio and Small Malaita, and eight ranger sites.

sources.title: Final project report: Developing the Mai-Maasina Green Belt for Malaita
sources.notes: Reports about 15,000 ha of customarily protected forest and growth from 10 to 30 members. Grantee-reported figures.

sources.title: Patterns of catch and trophic signatures illustrate diverse management requirements of coastal fisheries in Solomon Islands
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed. Covers Mararo (East Are'are), Hunanawa (Maramasike) and Liwe (Small Malaita), among 13 villages, with catch recorded in 2017.

sources.title: Community Based Resource Management in Malaita Province
sources.notes: Lists 32 place names on a map of community-based management in Malaita, including Mararo and Ahetaha (Manawai). Does not give constituencies.

sources.title: Conservation Division Continue To Support Groups Undertaking Conservation Initiatives
sources.notes: States five legally protected areas under the Protected Areas Act 2010 at that date, with Vuri the most recent.

sources.title: Conservation Groups in Malaita to Benefit USAID SCALE Project
sources.notes: Names Ahetaha Water Conservation Association and Takataka Eco-Village Conservation Foundation as grant recipients.

sources.title: Protected Areas Act 2010 (No. 4 of 2010)
sources.notes: Read via an automated summary. Check the full text before relying on section numbers or penalties.

sources.title: Electoral systems and boundaries
sources.notes: States the last redrawing of constituencies was in 1997 (47 to 50) and that a 2009 proposal to increase the number was rejected.

sources.title: CEPF grant: Developing a management and recovery plan for leatherback turtles in Are'are, Malaita
sources.notes: Wai-Hau Conservation Foundation; a species management plan for Wai-Hau and southern Malaita.
